title: Plan to Bring Tourists to Dublin's Neighbourhoods
summaryZh: 愛爾蘭觀光局計畫把遊客從市中心分散到都柏林其他街區。
paragraphs: Around six million tourists visit Dublin every year, but most of them stay in a small part of the city centre, between Christ Church Cathedral and Trinity College. Now the national tourism agency, Fáilte Ireland, wants to spread visitors more widely.

The agency is looking for a company to develop tourism in up to eight Dublin neighbourhoods. The project would begin with a pilot scheme in three areas, and it could later be extended if local businesses and residents support it.

According to the planning documents, the aim is to share the economic benefits of tourism with the wider city, while also strengthening local identity and encouraging communities to take part. Areas such as Stoneybatter, Phibsborough and the Liberties are known for their independent cafés, pubs and markets, which could attract curious visitors.

Not everyone is enthusiastic, however. Residents of busy tourist areas often complain about high prices and crowded footpaths, and some people worry that popular neighbourhoods could lose the character that made them attractive in the first place.

About six million tourists visit Dublin every year, but most of them stay in a small part of the city centre, between Christ Church Cathedral and Trinity College. Now Fáilte Ireland, the national tourism agency, wants visitors to go to other places too.

The agency wants a company to help bring tourists to up to eight Dublin neighbourhoods. First, it will try the idea in three areas. Later it could grow, if local shops and people who live there agree.

Some six million tourists descend on Dublin every year, yet the vast majority congregate in a compact stretch of the city centre between Christ Church Cathedral and Trinity College. Fáilte Ireland, the national tourism authority, now intends to disperse visitors more widely.

The agency is seeking a firm to cultivate tourism in up to eight Dublin neighbourhoods. The initiative would launch as a pilot in three areas and could subsequently be expanded, provided it wins the backing of local businesses and residents.

According to the tender documents, the objective is to distribute the economic benefits of tourism across the wider city, while reinforcing local identity and fostering community participation. Districts such as Stoneybatter, Phibsborough and the Liberties are renowned for their independent cafés, pubs and markets, which could appeal to more adventurous visitors.

The proposal has not been universally welcomed. Residents of tourist hotspots frequently lament soaring prices and congested footpaths, and some fear that sought-after neighbourhoods could be stripped of the very character that made them appealing.

Approximately six million tourists visit Dublin annually; however, the majority remain within a limited area of the city centre, between Christ Church Cathedral and Trinity College. Consequently, the national tourism agency, Fáilte Ireland, aims to distribute visitors more evenly across the capital.

The agency is seeking a company to develop tourism in up to eight Dublin neighbourhoods. The project would commence with a pilot scheme in three areas and could subsequently be expanded, contingent upon support from local businesses and residents.

The planning documents state that the objective is to share the economic benefits of tourism more equitably, while simultaneously strengthening local identity and encouraging community participation.
